candidates.desc: A Pixar-style craftsman in goggles gleefully smashes blue ceramic tiles with a hammer, breaking a whole stack into small shards; he accidentally knocks a clay pot off the bench so it shatters too, then arranges the broken pieces into a colorful mosaic sun.

In a sunlit stone courtyard, an animated boy holds a red apple high in the air, opens his hand and lets it fall. The apple bounces on the paving stones and he bends over his knees to look down at where it landed.

The tiled floor of a shop stacked with boxed toys is covered with dozens of black mousetraps, all set and laid out in rows. A man in a white shirt and shorts, blindfolded and holding a red foam bat, swings it around trying to hit a second man who is creeping between the traps in bare feet. The second man dodges away and steps carefully over the traps, but ends up sprawled on the floor among them while the blindfolded man swings again.

A quiet bedroom with pale green walls, a wooden bed, a rug and a bedside table with a red digital clock. A man lies stretched out on the bed. Suddenly the ceiling bursts open and an enormous steel coil spring shoots down through it, punching a ragged hole in the plasterboard and driving straight through the floorboards into another hole below. Broken laths and clouds of white mattress stuffing rain down over the room. The man is left face-down on the floor in the debris, then picks himself up, stands and brushes the fluff off his clothes.

A first-person shot from the seat of a red mobility scooter driving down an empty asphalt road between warehouses, straight into a low sun. The rider's hands are on the handlebars and a basket sits on the steering column. The steering column starts to come loose and sinks down; the basket and the handlebars drop away. In the last shots the scooter has come apart completely: a wheel, the basket, the red body panels and the handlebar lie scattered on the road in front of the rider, whose feet are still on the footplate.

A montage of people snatching things out of the air at the last moment. A young woman in a park pulls a falling tennis ball into her chest; a goalkeeper in green throws himself sideways and pins the ball to the grass in front of the goal; a young man in a kitchen shoots out a hand and grabs a plastic bottle before it hits the floor; a woman in a garden takes a whole watermelon out of the air with both hands; a boy lying on the grass stops a huge beach ball above his face with his hands and feet.

A fishing beach with a big wooden boat sitting high on timber skids. A crowd of villagers, men and women of all ages, put their shoulders and hands against the hull and shove it forward down the rollers towards the sea, straining with their heels dug into the sand. An old man in a blue shirt walks ahead of them hauling on a wooden beam and shouting the count. The boat runs down the skids and reaches the water, and the group ends up in a circle in the shallows, hugging each other and cheering.

A run of small mishaps, one after another. A black phone lies face down on a wooden kitchen floor where it has just landed. On a city pavement a girl holds an ice cream cone with only half a scoop left, the rest of it splattered pink on the ground beside her feet. In an office a woman in a blue blouse throws up her hands in panic as a whole file of white papers flies out of her arms and scatters through the air. In a kitchen a man's plastic bag splits and oranges, peaches and a jar roll out across the tiled floor. Finally a watermelon bursts open on a market street, pink flesh and juice sprayed in a wide splash, while shoppers jump back with their hands over their mouths.

A young man in a bucket hat kneels on the wet sand beside a tall, carefully carved sandcastle with towers, battlements and arched gates; kite surfers are out on the sea behind him. The surf runs in around the base of the castle. Each wave eats away more of it: first the outer walls slump, then the towers collapse one after another, until only a shapeless lump of wet sand and one small stump are left in the foam, and he sits back on his heels looking at it.

A young man in yellow waterproof dungarees stands in a small blue and orange wooden fishing boat on open sea below green cliffs. He leans right back with both hands on a fishing rod that is bent almost double, dragging the line up out of the water until a large silver fish breaks the surface on the hook and swings over the side of the boat. He then works a round landing net, hauling it up out of the water and swinging it in over a wooden crate on the deck, where several silver fish are already lying. At the end he lifts the full crate up towards the camera with both hands and grins.

A sunny street of brick terraced houses on moving day. A smiling young woman in a yellow top and black shorts walks along the pavement towards the camera, holding a heavy patterned armchair high above her head with just one hand, as if it weighed nothing. Behind her two young men bend and struggle to carry a mattress towards a moving van with its ramp down; one heaves it onto his shoulder. Cardboard boxes stand on the pavement and a tree grows by the road.
